parsed.explanation: Thin dossier on a small island state. The dominant facts are secondary per the rubric: unenforced male-sodomy provisions with a 2023 government report recording no enforcement, killings, torture or disappearances — no documented trans-specific targeting, police raids, facility bans, or border friction. But there is no documented trans acceptance (no third-gender tradition), no anti-discrimination law, documented discrimination across public services, and fear of prosecution inhibiting police reporting — a real exposure for a visitor needing police or services. Under rule 13 this sits between the 0.55 profiles (recurring service discrimination without documented societal hostility) and 0.65-C (dead-letter statute plus documented trans acceptance). The missing documented acceptance and the live statute's deterrent to reporting keep it a step below 0.65; no enforcement, no violence data, and no trans-specific exposure prevent it falling below 0.55. Open questions (border practice, custody) are unresolved but lighter than exposures.
